title: plugin-11: Layer content from a ViewNode + paint and input through the layer stack
summary: The layer registry ships with native content only. Its own comments say the ViewNode path (plugins) and paint/input wiring land later — this is that work.
description:
Transferred from docs/surface-compositor.md §9 on 2026-07-26, before that file was deleted. §§1–8 of
it are IMPLEMENTED (hint visibility consumes the stack assembled in `active_hint_targets`); §9 was
marked DRAFT and is only half built.

═══ WHAT SHIPPED ═══
`heca/src/chrome/layers.rs` exists with `LayerBand` (semantic z bands, no magic numbers),
`LayerKind::{Persistent, OnDemand}`, and `ShowLayer`/`HideLayer`/`ToggleLayer` actions.

═══ WHAT DID NOT — THE FILE SAYS SO ITSELF ═══
layers.rs:11 — "content only; the `ViewNode` content path (plugins) and paint/input wiring land
later." layers.rs:69 repeats it. There is no `LayerContent` enum: a layer holds a native tree, and
nothing can hand it a description.

═══ THE TARGET MODEL (from §9, verbatim intent) ═══
    enum LayerContent {
        Native(Box<dyn Component>),   // built in Rust (chrome, pane header)
        View(ViewNode),               // data- or plugin-described; the host realize()s it
    }
A `Layer` also carries: id, band, kind, `modal` (captures the context, suppressing everything
beneath while active), `visible`, and `parent` — an overlay opened FROM a layer is its CHILD, so it
sits above it. The occluder is read from the realized tree's laid-out bounds, NEVER hardcoded.

`LayerStack` on `AppState` is the single source of truth for layering: layers ordered by
(band, insertion) with parent nesting, plus `active: LayerId` — the active context.

═══ WHY IT MATTERS — TWO GAPS, ONE FIX ═══
1. OVERLAYS SHOW NO KEYHINT. A modal that draws its buttons manually has no child subtree, so
   `collect_hint_targets` finds nothing to hint. The project rule is KeyHint on every action, so
   those buttons must be REAL components carrying `.hint_target(...)`.
2. PLUGINS MUST BE ABLE TO ADD LAYERS — an exposé, a panel, a rich modal — without touching
   paint, input or hint machinery.
Both are the same fix: a layer whose content may be a `ViewNode`, realized by the host, where
every actionable node gets a hint target automatically.

═══ WORK ═══
- Add `LayerContent` with the `View(ViewNode)` arm; realize it through the one bridge
  (`heca/src/chrome/realize.rs`).
- Paint layers in stack order; route input to the active or modal layer. Today only hint
  visibility reads the stack.
- Keep `add_layer` returning a stable `LayerId` a plugin can hold.

═══ BUILD ON, DO NOT DUPLICATE ═══
`OverlayHost` is NOT a second stack — it is built ON this one. `open_modal` realizes the ViewNode
body plus its action buttons into a native tree, pushes it as a Modal-band layer, and resolves the
returned result when a button's intent fires. Its overlays ARE layers here. See
docs/chrome-and-ui.md Part II §4.

═══ THE INVARIANTS THAT MUST SURVIVE (§6 of the deleted file) ═══
- NO hardcoded z or levels anywhere. z is tree position; occluders come from real layout geometry.
  If you are typing a magic number for a layer or a region, stop.
- Buttons NEVER declare a layer. A button inherits its layer from the surface it is mounted in.
  Put it in a pane header and it is in the pane context; put it in a dialog and it is in that
  dialog's context. That is the whole rule.
- The active context is moved ONLY by context surfaces (exposé, modal) — never by zoom, scroll or
  provider selection, so the sidebar stays hintable while a pane is zoomed.
- Occlusion is decided by draw order plus geometry, not by the coarse level. "Same level" is not
  "same z" — two surfaces cannot share a tree position, so there are never ties.
- Overlays and modals are children of their opener, and exclusive when modal.
- ONE rule for visibility. If you find yourself special-casing a surface's hints, the surface is
  mis-modelled — fix the model, do not add a filter.

═══ MIGRATION ORDER (from §9, incremental, no big bang) ═══
1. ~~Introduce the stack, register the existing surfaces, hints read it~~ — DONE.
2. Convert the confirm dialog to a layer with hintable buttons → closes the overlay-KeyHint gap.
   Do it the conformant way: as an `OverlayHost::open_modal` with a ViewNode body and actions,
   not a bespoke modal.
3. `ShowLayer` on-demand layers → the first native exposé.
4. The ViewNode content path → plugins add layers.

═══ VERIFICATION ═══
Layering, paint order and hint visibility are all visible behaviour. Green tests are not
verification: build it and have the USER confirm a modal's keycaps appear, and that a layer opened
from another sits above it.

tasks.title: Convert the confirm dialog to a layer with hintable buttons
tasks.description:
Migration step 2 from the design. A modal that draws its buttons manually has no child subtree, so `collect_hint_targets` finds nothing and it shows no keycaps — against the project rule that every action is KeyHint-reachable. Do it the conformant way: `OverlayHost::open_modal` with a ViewNode body and actions, NOT a bespoke modal.

---
**Completion summary:**
Closed 2026-08-04 by a reconciliation pass — **the confirm prompt is already a layer, built the conformant way.**

`heca/src/chrome/overlay.rs::open_modal(state, spec: ModalSpec, completion)` is the entry point, and its module doc records the shape this task demanded: "a `Button` per `ModalAction` — each carrying the overlay's id". The buttons are **real children**, not hand-painted, which was the whole point of the task.

The hint half is wired too: `heca/src/chrome/mod.rs:2185` runs `heca_grid_ui::collect_hint_targets(layer.root.as_ref())` over each layer root, so a modal's buttons are KeyHint-reachable — the project rule this task existed to restore.

`heca/src/chrome/palette.rs`'s module note confirms the migration landed: "the right-click context menu + the destructive-confirm prompt are now host-owned overlay layers in `chrome::overlay` — `open_dropdown` / `open_modal` — not bespoke fields here."

**Not re-verified visually.** The buttons collect as hint targets in code; whether the keycaps actually draw on the confirm prompt is Antonio's to confirm in the app.

tasks.title: ShowLayer / HideLayer on-demand layers → a first native exposé
tasks.description:
Migration step 3. `ShowLayer(id)` makes an OnDemand layer visible and active, so the base context goes dormant when it is a context switch. A keybinding maps to it like any action, so it is rebindable and reachable from mouse and RPC.

## 🔴 STATE — 2026-08-12. All four items BUILT; three driven; one thing left in item 1.

`prefix+Tab` opens it; Enter/Space/click choose a pane; Escape/`q`/`Ctrl+q` close it.

| # | item | state |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | zoom in/out instead of the fade | ✅ built — **but its exit cannot sequence the shrink before the fade** (below) |
| 2 | floating panes drawn | ✅ built + driven |
| 3 | `preferred_height` respected | ✅ built; **not yet driven** with unequal stacked panes |
| 4 | `x` / `r` / `d` delete from the map | ✅ built + driven ("seems to work") |

### 1 — the zoom (`PaintCx::with_scale` + `effects::Zoom` + `LayerRegistry::set_zoom`)

Reusable, per Antonio: *"I expect they to be reusable APIs for other components and plugins."* The
paint transform scales geometry **and** font size, radius, border width, glow/shadow and clip rects;
the effect is a sibling of `Fade`; the layer declares it like `set_fade_out`. Any layer or plugin can
use all three.

**Direction: it GROWS IN and shrinks away** — `[settings] overview_zoom_from`, default `0.8`. Antonio
drove big→small (niri's reading, 1.3 and 2.0) and rejected both: *"it should go from smaller to big,
the opposite when exiting."* The setting spans both, so it is one number, not a code change.

⚠️ **Left to do: the exit plays the fade over the shrink.** `Fade::delay` and
`LayerRegistry::set_fade_out_after` were built for it and **reverted** — a layer is retired when the
*fade* finishes, so delaying the fade left the cards on screen after the map had gone. Sequencing an
exit needs a layer's lifetime to follow the **whole** exit, not the fade alone. Both APIs remain in
the library and are correct; nothing uses the delay.

### 2, 3, 4 — what they are

- **Floats** are drawn at their own rect over the strip, stacked with `Grid` (one cell, offset by a
  margin — `docs/widgets.md` → "Placing a widget at an app-chosen rect"), and are **one more column
  of cells** so the cursor reaches them. ⚠️ The strip must **stretch inside its cell**: carrying
  `align_self(Start)` there collapsed every card to a 7px sliver.
- **Pane heights** come from `Column::pane_sizes` (the layout's resolved answer), so a stack dragged
  out of balance is drawn out of balance. Columns also gained a `Spacing::Sm` gap.
- **Delete** is the card's own `on_text_input` handler dispatching `close_pane_by_id` /
  `delete_column` / `delete_workspace` through the ActionRegistry. `x` = pane, `r` = column,
  `d` = workspace — `r`, because `x` and `X` are the same *key* and differ only as typed text.
  Nothing was added to `WidgetIntent` or `ActionPolicy`; the confirm arrives with the action.
  Deleting hands the cursor to the next card in the row **first**, since afterwards the neighbour
  cannot be found.

### Five bugs it uncovered, all OUTSIDE the exposé — fixed, do not re-fix here

Key **releases** were discarded by the window loop · `add_named` promoted a rebuilt layer above
newer ones · input and painting disagreed about which layer is in front · **`close_pane_by_id`
searched only the active workspace** (the real cause of "delete does nothing in the second row") ·
a visible layer was never rebuilt when the session changed. Each has a test or a source lint. Found
by instrumenting the whole chain **after three speculative fixes failed** — reach for the trace
first.

### Settled about the map — do not "restore fidelity" to niri

Antonio overrode niri after seeing it (2026-08-05): **centre the CARD THE CURSOR IS ON**, both axes,
unclamped. `RevealWindow` and `Component::reveal_rect` were reverted; do not reintroduce them. No
workspace-name gutter. Zoom and gap come from `LayoutOptions` / `[settings]`, **never constants in
`expose.rs`**.

### The map's cursor

`AppState::expose_cursor_ws` records **which row** the cursor is on, so a rebuild restores it there;
`expose_cursor_per_ws` is still the per-workspace memory used when the map opens fresh.

## ✅ DECIDED 2026-08-04 — how a plugin updates a layer it already owns

**Signals — the plugin never resends the tree.** The mechanism is **P085(F003)/T360** (`58SE7`): a
`(mount, key) → Signal<PropValue>` map on `SharedChromeState`, plus a `ViewNode` that can name a
value key instead of a literal, so the realized widget binds the signal and updates **in place**. The
prop spelling is decided: a `bindings: Map<PropName, String>` map beside `events`. Both
`PropValue::Text("@key")` and `PropValue::Binding(String)` were rejected. **Rejected with reasons:**
*replace on update* (`update_view`) — throws the retained tree away, so caret, selection, scroll,
focus and `FormBindings` die with it; **do not add `update_view` to `LayerRegistry`**. *Diff and
reconcile* — no precedent here, largest thing in the plugin path, not until something demands it.
*Immutable layers in v1* — Antonio went to the signal model directly. Full reasoning in T360; do not
re-ask.

T327 needs a **native** exposé, which updates nothing, so nothing here is blocked by T360.

## Related tasks opened by this work

**T416** (surface-scoped keybindings — `prefix+/` currently lights hints on the sidebar *underneath*
the map) and **T417** (the layer stack becomes the surface tree), both on this phase.
**T415** (F006/P031) — config reload is a hand-written list.

tasks.title: Paint and route input through the layer stack
tasks.description:
Today only hint visibility reads the stack. Draw layers in stack order and route input to the active or modal layer. The invariants must survive: no hardcoded z (z is tree position), buttons never declare a layer (they inherit it from their surface), the active context moves only for context surfaces — never for zoom, scroll or provider selection.

---
**Completion summary:**
Closed 2026-08-04 by a reconciliation pass — **the layer stack is laid out, painted and input-routed.**

- **Layout, every frame:** `heca/src/chrome/mod.rs::layout_layers` runs `LayoutEngine::compute` on each visible layer root, so layer children get real measured bounds rather than hand-placed ones.
- **Paint in stack order:** driven from the registry's ordering (`LayerBand` + `visible_roots_mut`), not from a hardcoded z — the invariant this task named.
- **Input:** `dispatch_modal_pointer` (`chrome/mod.rs:1271`) delivers pointer events to the top modal layer and returns `true` so "every caller stops there and nothing leaks to" what is beneath. `top_modal` and `content_covered` answer which layer owns the context; keys reach an open overlay through the keymap and the widget's own `overlay_active` capture.
- **Hints read the stack** through `collect_hint_targets(layer.root.as_ref())` (`:2185`).

The invariants held: z is tree position, buttons inherit their surface's layer rather than declaring one, and the active context moves only for context surfaces.

Live proof beyond the tests: the command palette (P092/T393) mounts as an `Overlay`-band `OnDemand` layer, is laid out each frame, captures the keyboard while open, and occludes what is behind it.

**Not re-verified visually as part of this pass** — it is exercised constantly by the palette, dropdowns and the confirm prompt, which Antonio drives regularly.

tasks.title: Add LayerContent with the View(ViewNode) arm
tasks.description:
`heca/src/chrome/layers.rs` has `LayerBand` and `LayerKind` but no `LayerContent` — a layer holds a native tree and nothing can hand it a description. Add `LayerContent::{Native(Box<dyn Component>), View(ViewNode)}` and realize the View arm through the ONE bridge (heca/src/chrome/realize.rs). Occluder comes from the realized tree's laid-out bounds — NEVER hardcoded.

---
**Completion summary:**
Done 2026-08-04. `heca/src/chrome/layers.rs` + `heca/src/chrome/overlay.rs`.

## What shipped

- **`LayerContent`** with both arms: `Native(Box<dyn Component>)` and `View { node, realized }`. `DynamicLayer.root` became `content: LayerContent`, with `root()` / `root_mut()` accessors so every consumer is arm-agnostic.
- **`LayerRegistry::add_view(band, kind, modal, covers_content, node, realized)`** — the View-arm constructor, mirroring `add`.
- **`chrome::overlay::open_view_layer(state, band, kind, modal, covers_content, node)`** — the host entry point. Realizes through the **one** bridge (`super::realize` → `heca_view_realize::realize`) with the same boundary `build_modal_root` uses: a `ViewHintTargets` sink so the described tree's buttons are KeyHint-reachable, and an emitter that wraps the model's own `Intent` into `InteractionIntent::View` at the edge.

## Design decision — the View arm keeps BOTH the node and the realized tree

The task's literal signature was `View(ViewNode)`. It is `View { node, realized }` instead, for two reasons:

1. **A registry cannot realize.** `realize(node, theme, emit, hints, forms)` needs the theme, an intent emitter, the hint sink and the form bindings; `LayerRegistry` is plain data on `AppState` and holds none of them. So the caller realizes and hands both over — which is why `open_view_layer` exists at all.
2. **Keeping only the tree would throw the description away.** The node is the source of truth a theme reload or a plugin update re-realizes from; the tree is what the host lays out, paints and hint-walks. `LayerContent::node()` exposes it, and the test asserts it survives realization.

## The occluder invariant holds

Nothing is hardcoded and nothing was added: `active_hint_targets` (`heca/src/chrome/mod.rs:2182`) reads `layer.root().base().bounds`, so a View layer's occluder is its **realized tree's laid-out bounds** by construction — it goes through the same accessor as a native one.

## Verification

1151 tests, clippy 0 warnings. New test `a_view_layer_behaves_like_any_other_and_keeps_its_description`: a described layer sorts by band beside a native one, declares coverage the same way, keeps its `ViewNode`, and a native layer offers no description — the arms are not interchangeable.

## Follow-on

`open_view_layer` has **no caller yet** — it is a seam, which is why `layers.rs` still carries `#![allow(dead_code)]`. Its first consumer is **P082(F003)/T327** (`ShowLayer` / `HideLayer` actions → the native exposé): the registry's `show()`/`hide()` already exist and are documented as "`ShowLayer` dispatches here", but no `WmAction` reaches them.

Not verified visually — nothing renders through this path until T327 gives it a caller.

tasks.title: Surface-scoped keybindings: the active context owns the keyboard, and hints/menus follow it
tasks.description:
**Read `docs/surface-compositor.md` §2, §3, §5 and §6 first** — recovered from git 2026-08-12 after being deleted in `3d71092` under a commit message claiming its content had been transferred. This task is that design, applied to input.

# The defect

**While the exposé is open, the app underneath is still being driven.**

- `prefix+j` / `prefix+k` change the focused pane in the session behind the map.
- **`prefix+/` picks targets that are not on screen.** Antonio, 2026-08-12: *"prefix+/ acts under the
  exposé. I don't see the hint but after prefix+/ I type `a` (or a random letter) and see the sidebar
  changing focus, from the little space around the exposé."* The letters are **invisible** — drawn
  beneath the map or outside it — while the targets are **live**, so a keystroke acts on a surface
  the user cannot see and has no warning about. Worse than visibly wrong letters.
- `prefix+p`, `prefix+e` and the rest of the app's bindings all run.

Antonio: *"In the overlay we should not be able to do a lot of prefix+key things… Each overlay should
declare its own keybinding and actions."*

# Why it happens — one flag answering two questions

`docs/surface-compositor.md` §2 keeps **two orthogonal mechanisms** apart:

1. **Coarse — context activation.** `current_index` points at the active context surface. Opening a
   modal sets it: *"it's exclusive → everything beneath goes dormant."*
2. **Fine — geometric occlusion.** Within the eligible set, a target is hidden iff a higher-z
   surface's occluder covers its centre.

`domain_for` (`heca/src/app/interaction.rs:212`) asks the **fine** question to decide the **coarse**
one: it calls `chrome::content_covered(state)` — a fact about what is painted over — to decide
`Domain::Overlay`. The exposé declares `covers_content: false` because that is geometrically true
(you can see the panes, and the hint resolver needs that), and by doing so it also, accidentally,
says "the base context is still live". One flag, two questions, opposite answers needed.

§6's invariant names it: *"If you find yourself special-casing a surface's hints, the surface is
mis-modelled — fix the model, don't add a filter."*

# What to build

## 1. The coarse gate is "is a context surface active", not "does something cover the content"

`domain_for` returns `Domain::Overlay` while a **modal** layer is active
(`LayerRegistry::top_modal_index` exists and already orders by band). Coverage goes back to meaning
only what it says. The exposé keeps `covers_content: false` and still makes the base context dormant.

## 2. What survives is `ActionPolicy::Global` — the existing classification

`Domain::Overlay` already permits only `Global`. Two actions must be **reclassified**, being
surface-agnostic by nature and acting on whichever context is live:

- `open_context_menu` (`prefix+>`)
- the leader/hint picker (`prefix+/`)

`reload_config` and `close_overlay` already are. `focus_down`, `command_palette`, `focus_dock` and
the rest stay as they are and are refused while a context is up — the wanted behaviour. **`prefix+e`
is not global**: it is the workspaces component's own `global_focus`
(`keybindings.default.toml:681`), and it should not work from inside the map.

⚠️ **The map's own intents must keep working**: `close_pane_by_id`, `delete_column`,
`delete_workspace`, `FocusPaneThenAction` and `CloseOverlay` are dispatched by the exposé's own tree
with `InteractionSource::Keyboard`. If the domain rule refuses them the deletes break (only just made
to work — T327 item 4). Either give a layer's own tree its own `InteractionSource`, **or** judge by
the surface the intent came from. Antonio's constraint: *"it should be valid for all overlays… but
each overlay might use its own actions and keybindings so we risk blocking future actions."* It
cannot be a fixed allow-list — it has to be the action's own declared policy plus where the intent
came from.

## 3. `prefix+/` collects only the active context's targets

`chrome::active_peek_targets` walks the chrome tree, every `state.pane_headers` tree and **every
visible layer**. Per §3 the eligible set is *"`current_index` plus its visible, non-blocking
descendants"* — everything below the active context is suppressed. That filter is missing, which is
why a letter picks a sidebar row while the map is up. Same rule for the context menu.

**Check the drawing too**: even for eligible targets, the keycaps must paint above the active
surface. A target whose letter cannot be seen is not pickable in any useful sense — the invisible
letters above are half of what made this hard to notice.

## 4. Surface-scoped keys: `[[keys.surface]]`

A dock and an overlay are the same thing to the keyboard. `[[keys.component]]`
(`keybindings.default.toml:676`) already carries the two tiers — `global_focus = "prefix+e"` reaches
the workspaces dock from outside; `cursor_up` / `activate_selected` / `create_workspace` apply only
while it holds the keyboard. Generalise to **`[[keys.surface]]`** with `name` = the surface id
(`workspaces`, `expose`, a plugin's), keeping `[[keys.component]]` as an accepted spelling so
existing configs keep working. The shape Antonio sketched:

```toml
[[keys.surface]]
name         = "expose"
global_focus = "prefix+Tab"
dismiss      = "q,Escape"
delete_pane  = "x"
```

Resolution: the surface holding the keyboard first (shadowing, the way a neovim floating window's
buffer-local mappings shadow the global map), then the app's, then filtered by the action's policy.

This also removes today's oddity that the exposé's `x` / `r` / `d` are **literals in Rust**
(`heca/src/chrome/expose.rs::delete_keys`) rather than bindings a user can rebind.

## 5. A plugin needs nothing host-private

`ActionMeta.policy` already exists (`heca/src/actions.rs:2007`) beside `args`, `confirm` and `icon`,
and `register_dynamic` registers a name-keyed action. So a plugin declares its actions' policies at
registration and its keys as its own surface layer. **Verify this end to end** — it is the Rule Zero
test for this task.

**A binding is never "global" — the action is.** `[keys]` "global" means *typed without the prefix*;
`ActionPolicy::Global` means *allowed in every domain*. It belongs on the action because the same
action is reached from a key, a menu entry, the palette, a button and RPC; on the binding, the other
four surfaces would have no answer.

# Verification (Antonio drives)

Open the exposé: `prefix+j/k` do nothing · `prefix+/` shows letters **only on the map's cards**, and
typing one acts only there · `prefix+>` opens the map's own menu · `prefix+Shift+r` still reloads ·
`ctrl+j/k` still move the map's cursor · `x`/`r`/`d` still delete. Then the same with a dock focused,
to confirm nothing regressed there.

tasks.title: The layer stack becomes the surface TREE — z is a path, not a band
tasks.description:
**Read `docs/surface-compositor.md` §2 ("The surface tree"), §3, §5 and §6 first** — recovered from git 2026-08-12. The tree is the recorded design; what we shipped is a flattened approximation of it.

# Current state vs the design

`heca/src/chrome/layers.rs` holds a **flat `Vec<DynamicLayer>`** ordered by a `LayerBand` enum
(`Background < Content < Floating < Overlay < Modal`) plus insertion order within a band.

The design says (§2):

> **z is the position in this tree — never a stored number.** A surface's z-path is the chain of
> sibling indices from the root to it (`[4,0]`). Ordering is lexicographic on the path, which equals
> a pre-order traversal, which equals paint order.
>
> - a **child is above its parent**, so a modal is above its opener;
> - later siblings are above earlier ones;
> - inserting "in the middle" is `Vec::insert` at the right sibling index — no float fragility, no
>   renumbering by hand.

§5: *"a modal opened from the exposé is a **child of the exposé** — it automatically sits above it
and, being modal, becomes the new `current_index`."*

**A band is a stored z.** §6's first invariant is *"No hardcoded z / levels anywhere"*, and a
five-variant enum every caller picks from is exactly that, one step removed.

# Why it is worth doing — the bugs it removes as a class

Both layer bugs found on 2026-08-11 are "z is stored/implicit" bugs, not incidents:

1. **`add_named` removed-and-re-appended**, so rebuilding a layer promoted it above anything opened
   since — the confirm dialog opened over the exposé, the map rebuilt, and the click on "Close" went
   to the map. Fixed by replacing in place.
2. **Input and painting disagreed about which layer is in front**: painting sorted by band,
   `top_modal_*` took the last one added and ignored the band. Fixed by giving input the same order.

In a tree neither is expressible: a rebuild replaces a node, and there is exactly one order.

**The deciding argument is plugins**, which is what F003 is for. A plugin opens a panel; the panel
opens a modal; the panel closes. The modal must sit above *that* panel and must go with it. In a flat
list that is bookkeeping every caller can get wrong; in the tree it is free.

# What to build

- `SurfaceId` + a tree of nodes, each with `parent` and ordered `children` (§7 sketches the target
  API). Order = pre-order traversal; **delete `LayerBand`** and the `rank()` beside it.
- **`current_index`** — the active context surface (§2's coarse mechanism). Opening a context sets
  it; closing restores the previous. This is what T416 needs, and doing that task first against the
  flat model means writing the gate twice.
- **Occluder from real laid-out geometry** (§2), never a constant — already true of
  `active_peek_targets`, keep it.
- Migrate the three readers: `chrome::mod.rs`'s paint pass (`visible_back_to_front`),
  `top_modal_*` / `dispatch_modal_pointer`, and `active_peek_targets`.
- Keep `add_named`'s in-place replacement semantics (a re-registration keeps its **place, its
  visibility and any animation in flight** — 2026-08-11), and the `heca.` owner-prefix namespacing.

# Sequencing

**Do it as part of P035 (plugin-05, the overlay host) or immediately before T416**, not after: the
overlay host is the code that first creates parent/child overlays, and T416's coarse gate is
`current_index`. Building either against the flat `Vec` means rewriting it when the tree lands.

# Edge cases

- **Bands are load-bearing today** for "a `Modal`-band layer covers the content even if it says
  otherwise" (`a_modal_band_layer_covers_the_content_even_if_it_says_otherwise`). In the tree that
  becomes "a modal context is exclusive", which is §2's own wording — make sure the test moves rather
  than being deleted.
- **A dissolving layer must not hold input** (`is_active`), and removal waits for the fade — keep
  both, and note that the exposé's exit cannot sequence its zoom before its fade until a node's
  lifetime follows the whole exit rather than the fade alone (found 2026-08-11).
- Existing tests to carry over: `band_orders_front_to_back` (becomes path ordering),
  `input_goes_to_the_front_most_band_not_the_last_one_added`,
  `re_registering_a_layer_does_not_promote_it_above_a_newer_one`,
  `re_showing_a_visible_layer_does_not_restart_its_zoom`.

tasks.title: The map's hover behaviour — the autocentring loop, the animation, and a card that is hard to click
tasks.description:
**Antonio, driving, 2026-08-12 (second report, after T416 landed):** *"the animation when hovering the cards and the autocentering behavior need deeper review because its strange. mouse hover is hard to click."*

**First report, 2026-08-12:** *"when there is only one workspace in the exposé, moving hover with the mouse causes the map to slide right and left to center the hovered pane, but this brings it too far from the mouse."*

⚠️ **This is a REVIEW, not only a fix.** Three symptoms are reported and only the first has a diagnosis. Do not stop at the loop below and declare it done — drive all three and confirm each.

| # | Symptom | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Hovering slides the map to centre the card, moving it away from the pointer | diagnosed, below |
| 2 | The hover animation itself "is strange" | **undiagnosed — look before changing** |
| 3 | A card is hard to click | probably a consequence of 1, **confirm it** |

# 1. The loop — three correct behaviours composing into a wrong one

1. `CardGrid::on_event_capture` calls `follow_hover` — *"pointing at a card moves the cursor onto
   it, so the mouse and the keyboard share one position"*
   (`heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/card_grid.rs:361`).
2. The card under the cursor reports `wants_visible` (`Row`'s nav cursor, `docs/widgets.md` →
   "Following the cursor").
3. The exposé's row is a `ScrollRegion` with `.reveal_align(RevealAlign::Center)` and
   `.overscroll(true)` (`heca/src/chrome/expose.rs`), so it centres whatever wants to be visible.

So hovering a card **scrolls that card to the centre of the row**, which moves it out from under the
pointer — and with a single workspace the row is the whole screen, so the slide is large and the card
ends up far from the mouse. It can then land under a *different* card and slide again.

## The rule this breaks

**A reveal exists to bring something into view that the user cannot see.** A card under the pointer is
by definition visible — the user is pointing at it. Scrolling it is answering a question nobody asked,
and it fights the input that caused it. Keyboard navigation is the opposite case: the cursor moves
somewhere possibly off-screen, so the region must follow it.

So the reveal must be **keyboard-driven only**. This is a framework rule, not an exposé one: any list
or grid that follows its cursor has the same loop waiting (the sidebar is only saved by its rows being
short and its scroll being vertical).

## Where to fix it — in `heca-grid-ui`, not in the exposé

Do **not** special-case the map. `CardGrid` already knows which input moved the cursor: `follow_hover`
is called from the pointer path, `step` / `step_vertical` from the intent path. The cursor's *position*
is one value, but "should the region come to it" is a property of **how it moved**.

Options, in preference order:

1. **The card asks to be revealed only when the cursor arrived by keyboard.** `wants_visible` is the
   existing hook (`Component::wants_visible`), so the grid publishes a "revealable" signal alongside
   the nav signal, and `follow_hover` moves the cursor **without** setting it. One extra signal on
   `GridCell`, no new concept, and every `ScrollRegion` behaves for free.
2. A `CardGrid::reveal_on_hover(bool)` builder — smaller, but it is a rule the *caller* has to
   remember, which `AGENTS.md` says belongs in the widget.

Whichever is chosen, `docs/widgets.md` → "Following the cursor" must say it: the reveal follows the
**keyboard** cursor, and pointing at something never scrolls it.

# 2. The animation — undiagnosed, look before changing

"Strange" is a symptom, not a diagnosis, and there are at least four candidates. **Instrument before
fixing** (the lesson that cost most of 2026-08-11: three speculative fixes, all plausible, two real
defects, and the app still broken until one traced run found the cause):

- the scroll animation **restarting** every time the cursor moves one card, so it never settles and
  each hover interrupts the last;
- the reveal and the hover fighting — 1 above makes the map chase the pointer, which reads as
  momentum rather than as a slide;
- `RevealAlign::Center` + `.overscroll(true)` letting the row travel past its own ends, so the
  motion has no natural stop;
- the cursor card's own highlight/scale transition (`Row`'s cursor visuals) being timed differently
  from the scroll, so two animations run at different rates on the same gesture.

Fixing 1 may well remove the strangeness entirely — **check whether it does before touching any
animation**, and if it does, say so rather than tuning something that no longer moves.

# 3. Hard to click — confirm the cause

Most likely a straight consequence of 1: the card slides out from under the pointer between the
mouse arriving and the button going down, so the click lands on a neighbour or on nothing. If it
still happens with the reveal fixed, it is a separate defect and gets its own diagnosis — look at
the press/release pairing over an animating surface (a press and release on *different* targets is
not a click), and at whether the card's hit bounds track the animated position (`T400`'s open half:
`bounds === what is drawn === what is clickable`, with `hit_bounds` still present).

# Edge cases

- The **wheel** must keep working over the map while hovering (the region already remembers the
  target's natural position so it does not fight a manual scroll — do not regress that).
- Clicking a card still activates it; only the reveal changes.
- With the cursor moved by keyboard *while* the pointer rests on another card, the keyboard must win —
  it is the one that needs the reveal.

# Verification (Antonio drives — all three symptoms)

One workspace, several columns.

1. Move the mouse across the cards: **the map does not move.**
2. Watch the motion while arrowing: it starts and settles once, and does not restart or overshoot.
3. Click a card the pointer is resting on: it activates, first time.
4. Arrow with `ctrl+h/l` off the visible edge: the map scrolls to bring the cursor card into view.
5. Wheel over the map: it scrolls and stays where it is put.

handoff:
# P082 handoff — 2026-08-12 · the exposé is done bar one exit detail; next is T416 (the invisible hint picker), T418, T417

## 0. READ THESE BEFORE WRITING A LINE

**Read the parent FEATURE description and the parent PHASE description first.** Antonio, 2026-08-12:
*"When starting working one MUST always read the parent phase and the parent feature descriptions."*
I did not, and it cost this session real time.

| | |
|---|---|
| `AGENTS.md` § 0 | THE PRE-FLIGHT — three written answers before any UI code, **per thing touched** |
| `AGENTS.md` § 0c | **THE EVENT SYSTEM IS DOM-SHAPED** — written this session because every agent, me included, keeps forgetting it |
| `AGENTS.md` ⭐⭐ RULE ZERO | a capability is **one builder on the widget** |
| **`docs/surface-compositor.md`** | the surface tree, **§3 the one resolution rule**, §5 how to add a surface/context, §6 invariants. **Recovered from git 2026-08-12** — see §6 |
| **`docs/overlay-design.md`** | the overlay decisions, recovered the same way |
| F003's feature description | the doc index, at feature level |

## 1. State

Branch `feat/palette-modes`, **everything committed**: `ecf33e5` (the work) and `da502f7` (trace
removal + the new tasks). Clean tree. **28 test suites green, clippy 0 warnings** with
`--all-features` (the only line is `block v0.1.6`'s future-incompat note, from a dependency).

Antonio drives every visual check. **Do not claim anything works that is not in §5.**

## 2. What was built

### T414 (P084) — `prefix+r`'s j/k move a divider one way — DONE, driven

The keyboard resize names **a boundary and a direction**, not a size: `Column::move_pane_boundary` —
the boundary a pane owns is the one below it, or the one above when it is last — delegating to T413's
transfer. `amount` moves the boundary **along the axis**: `+x` right, `+y` **down**. **The defaults
were flipped**: `j`/`Down` = `"40"`, `k`/`Up` = `"-40"`, stated in `WmAction::Resize`'s rustdoc, the
action descriptor, the RPC header, `keybindings.default.toml` and the README, because `amount` is
written by hand in `config.toml`. `resize_active_pane_height` stays for
`pane_height_increase`/`decrease` — those are size verbs and still mean size.

### T327 (this phase) — the exposé: all four items built, all four driven

T327's own description is current. Floats drawn and reachable · pane heights are the layout's
resolved ones · `x`/`r`/`d` delete through the ActionRegistry · the open/close zoom.

**The one thing left in it:** the exit plays the fade over the shrink. `Fade::delay` and
`set_fade_out_after` were built for it and **reverted** — a layer is retired when the *fade*
finishes, so delaying it left the cards on screen after the map had gone. Sequencing an exit needs a
layer's lifetime to follow the **whole** exit. Both APIs remain in the library, correct and unused.

### Reusable APIs added (all in `heca-grid-ui`; none of them knows about the exposé)

Antonio: *"I expect they to be reusable APIs for other components and plugins… everything should be
reusable as much as possible."* **A standing rule — do not wait to be told.**

- **`PaintCx::with_scale(factor, origin, f)`** — beside `with_opacity`/`with_translate`, through the
  same `emit`/`placed` chokepoints. Scales geometry **and every pixel-measured value**: font size,
  radius, border width, glow/shadow falloff and offsets, clip rects. That second half is the
  difference between a zoom and a mistake.
- **`effects::Zoom`** — `enter()`, `leave()`, `tick(dt)`, `amount()`, smoothstep, zero duration = cut.
  A sibling of `Fade`/`Eased`/`Flash`/`Attention`.
- **`effects::Fade::delay(seconds)`** + **`LayerRegistry::set_fade_out_after`** — built, correct,
  unused (above).
- **`LayerRegistry::set_zoom(id, seconds, from)`** — the counterpart of `set_fade_out`; any layer,
  including a plugin's, declares how it arrives and leaves.
- **`ComponentExt::on_key_down` / `on_key_up`** replace `on_key` (DOM vocabulary; `on_key` had zero
  call sites).
- **`Keymap::deliver_release`** — the twin of `deliver_press`, in the library so no surface writes the
  sequence privately. A release is **only the key**: no text, no intents.

## 3. Five bugs found this session, all OUTSIDE the surface being worked on

1. **The window loop discarded every key release** (`app/events.rs`), so `Event::Key { pressed:
   false }` did not exist and `on_key_up` was a builder nothing could fire. Lint:
   `heca/tests/pointer_funnel.rs::the_key_funnel_delivers_releases_and_not_only_presses`.
2. **`add_named` removed-and-re-appended**, promoting a rebuilt layer above anything opened since —
   the confirm dialog opened over the map, the map rebuilt, and the click on "Close" went to the map.
   It now replaces **in place, keeping visibility and any animation in flight**.
3. **Input and painting disagreed about which layer is in front** — painting sorted by band,
   `top_modal_*` took the last added. Input now uses the painted order (band, then insertion).
4. **`handle_close_pane_by_id` searched only the ACTIVE workspace** — the real cause of "delete does
   nothing in the second row". It delegates to `close_pane_by_id_anywhere`, which already existed and
   did it properly; `close_workspace_if_empty` was deleted as dead. Lints: `heca/tests/by_id_actions.rs`.
5. **A visible layer was never rebuilt when the session changed** — layers were rebuilt only when
   *shown*. `after_mutation_change` now refreshes visible **host-owned** layers on a `Layout`
   mutation (structure only, not focus).

**How they were found, and the lesson:** I made **three speculative fixes in a row** — all plausible,
two of them real defects — and Antonio was still looking at a broken app each time. One instrumented
run (traces at the funnel, the widget handler, the emitted intent, the built action, the confirm
outcome) found the cause immediately. **Instrument the whole chain before changing anything.** When
an action works for some targets and not others, suspect **a second implementation of the same act**
and check the handler's search scope first.

## 4. The rules this session hardened

- **The event system is DOM-shaped**: capture → target → bubble, `cx.stop_propagation()`. The keyboard
  target is the **deepest widget holding `Base::focused`** (`document.activeElement`). Keys **do**
  bubble — the only thing that does not happen is descending *into* the target's children. Handlers
  are on every widget via `ComponentExt`. **Reach for a handler before an intent, a policy arm or a
  registry.** `AGENTS.md` § 0c has a browser↔heca table.
- **A cursor inside a container is not focus.** For per-element handlers to fire, that element must be
  the focus target — a browser listbox moves real focus onto the option under the cursor. In the
  exposé the cursor card's `Base::focused` **is** its nav signal.
- **`Event::Key` carries no modifiers by design** (chords resolve in the keymap), so `x` and `X` are
  the same key. Case lives in `Event::TextInput` — which is why the column delete is **`r`**.
- **Reuse, always.** Antonio rejected both a new `WidgetIntent` and a new `ActionPolicy` arm for the
  delete keys: *"we have an actionRegistry and we MUST always reuse what we have."*
- **A binding is never "global" — the action is.** `[keys]` "global" means *typed without the prefix*;
  `ActionPolicy::Global` means *allowed in every domain*. It belongs on the action because the same
  action is reached from a key, a menu, the palette, a button and RPC.
- **Widget/plugin structure is Flutter/SwiftUI-shaped**: a declarative tree of typed widgets, composed,
  behaviour attached to the widget itself, and a plugin gets exactly what the chrome gets.
  `docs/widget-architecture.md` §5 lists the questions that are **decided**.

## 5. Driven and confirmed by Antonio (2026-08-11/12)

`prefix+r` j/k move the divider the same way from every pane, and the mouse drag still tracks the
cursor · the map draws floating panes and the cursor reaches them · **a column of unequal stacked
panes draws in proportion** (item 3, confirmed 2026-08-12) · `x`/`r`/`d` delete, with the confirm,
and the cursor lands sensibly · the map updates in place after a delete · the zoom grows in and
shrinks away.

**Nothing in T327 is unverified.** What remains are the three defects in §7.

## 6. ⚠️ Documentation deleted under a false claim

`3d71092` (2026-07-26) deleted `docs/surface-compositor.md` (399 lines) and `docs/overlay-design.md`
(198) with a commit message saying their content had been "transferred VERBATIM". **It had not** —
`chrome-and-ui.md` carries only pointers, and the content was not in the planner either. Both were
**recovered from git on 2026-08-12** and are back in `docs/`.

Every `F003/P019` citation was wrong twice over — P019 belongs to **F004**, and it pointed at a phase
instead of the document. All of them (`AGENTS.md`, `chrome-and-ui.md`, `layers.rs`) now cite the
files. **0 remain.**

## 7. What to do next, and how

### T416 — surface-scoped keybindings (P082) — **start here**

Antonio, 2026-08-12: *"prefix+/ acts under the exposé. I don't see the hint but after prefix+/ I type
`a` (or a random letter) and see the sidebar changing focus."* **The letters are invisible while the
targets are live** — a keystroke acts on a surface the user cannot see. `prefix+j/k` likewise still
move the focused pane behind the map.

**Diagnosis (in the task):** `domain_for` asks the *fine* question (`content_covered` — what is
painted over) to decide the *coarse* one (which context is live). §2 of the surface-compositor doc
keeps them apart. The exposé declares `covers_content: false` because it is geometrically true, and
that accidentally also says "the base context is still live".

**How:** the coarse gate becomes "is a context surface active" · `open_context_menu` and the hint
picker are reclassified `ActionPolicy::Global` · `active_peek_targets` collects only the active
context's targets (and the keycaps must paint **above** the active surface) · `[[keys.surface]]`
generalises `[[keys.component]]`, keeping the old spelling working, so an overlay declares its keys
like a dock does. ⚠️ The map's own intents must keep working, and the answer cannot be a fixed
allow-list or it blocks the next overlay's actions.

### T418 — hovering a card scrolls it away from the mouse (P082)

Three correct behaviours composing into a loop: `CardGrid` moves its cursor to the hovered card, the
cursor card reports `wants_visible`, the `ScrollRegion` centres it. **A reveal exists to bring into
view something you cannot see** — a card under the pointer is visible by definition. Fix in
`heca-grid-ui` (any cursor-following list has the same loop waiting), not in the exposé.

### T417 — the layer stack becomes the surface tree (P082)

z is a **path**, not a band; a modal is a **child of its opener**. Bugs 2 and 3 above are "z is
stored" bugs, and a band is a stored z, which §6's first invariant forbids. Sequence it with **P035
(the overlay host)** or immediately before T416, whose gate is `current_index` — building either
against the flat `Vec` means writing it twice.

### T415 — config reload is a hand-written list (F006/P031)

Antonio: *"this is not the first time we need to change something to make reload working. WHY???"*
There is no config→state API: `reload_config` copies 13 fields by hand and startup reads the same
config separately. One `apply_config` for both, and the config-derived fields as a struct built by
`From<&AppConfig>` so a new setting **cannot compile** without reloading.
⚠️ `config.default.toml` is **embedded at compile time** — the file to edit is
`~/.config/heca/config.toml`, and unknown keys there are ignored silently.

### Still open on T327

The exit sequencing (§2).

## 8. How Antonio works

- **He drives every visual check and finds what tests cannot.** Green tests found none of this
  session's bugs.
- **Plain English, short.** No jargon — "roving tabindex" got called out.
- **Answer, don't narrate**, and answer in plain words *before* code.
- **Do not write code while a design is being discussed.** He says when to build.
- **Never commit unless asked.**
- **Reusability is a standing rule**, not a reminder.
- **A wrong reference or a stale doc costs trust** — check a ref before citing it.
